required_denominator: annual Boeing family/cohort departures or sectors for 2010-2025 under a compatible global commercial-jet scope, with source-vintage/revision semantics sufficient for reproducible historical baseline construction

sources.source_title: Aviation Data Repository for Research / Data API
sources.observed_granularity: research-access flight records and trajectories with aircraft type, operator, route and market segment; primarily European network
sources.reason: Potentially useful for an independently observed European sensitivity series (2015-2024), but registration/access is required and coverage is not global. It cannot replace the global denominator.

sources.observed_granularity: periodic airport-to-airport flight stages by departures, service type, airline and aircraft type for reporting European countries
sources.reason: Official downloadable aircraft-type flight-stage data can strengthen a European cross-check. Coverage is limited to reporting countries/airports and cannot represent global exposure.

sources.observed_granularity: monthly Canadian airport movements with aircraft type/designator and movement details
sources.reason: Official open data can provide a long Canadian cross-check by type, but does not cover global operations and airport coverage varies by reporting facility.

sources.source_title: Australian Aircraft Activity and Flight Summary Data
sources.observed_granularity: annual Australian activity and bulk flight movements with ICAO aircraft type, operator and movement type
sources.reason: Public Australian time series and flight-summary products can validate type-level activity, but geographic scope is Australia and historical bulk-flight completeness must be checked.

sources.source_title: Open-source traffic and CO2 emission dataset
sources.observed_granularity: 2019 origin-destination-operator-aircraft tuples with route capacity and aircraft type where available
sources.reason: Useful for a 2019 route/type context check, but assembled from limited-coverage open sources and does not provide complete performed departures or a versioned global denominator.

sources.observed_granularity: observed aircraft states/trajectories with incomplete global and historical coverage
sources.reason: Useful for spot checks and fleet activity sensitivity, but ADS-B reception, transponder use and historical retention are non-uniform. Observed tracks are not a complete global exposure denominator.

sources.source_title: Annual Safety Report sector data + World Air Transport Statistics (WATS)
sources.observed_granularity: public model-level global annual sectors in historical Annex 4 editions through 2019; later public Safety Reports expose aggregate jet/turboprop and regional sectors; current WATS product advertises longitudinal aircraft/model utilization
sources.reason: The 2019 Safety Report Annex 4 publicly provides annual sectors by manufacturer/model for 2015-2019, continuing overlapping public Annex 4 windows back to at least 2010. In later inspected public reports the former manufacturer/model matrix is not continuously available. WATS Global is proprietary and remains an access candidate rather than a demonstrated baseline. Historical Safety Report sector figures are revision-sensitive.

sources.observed_granularity: licensed global historical schedule/flight records with aircraft/equipment information and historical schedule-version semantics
sources.reason: Technically promising for a reproducible global model-year matrix, but no licensed BSFM access or representative product extract is connected. Exact fields, performed-flight semantics, 737 variant mapping, cargo/charter scope and licence constraints must be audited before use.

sources.source_title: Historical Flight Status / Schedules / Fleet and Values
sources.observed_granularity: historical flight-status data documented from 2006-02-07 with equipment type and scheduled/actual timing; more than 20 years of historical schedules; aircraft utilization/cycle products also available
sources.reason: Cirium documents global commercial flight/schedule products with history extending before 2010 and aircraft/equipment information. It is nevertheless proprietary. The exact licensed product, global performed-flight completeness, passenger/cargo/charter scope, deterministic BSFM cohort mapping, cancellation semantics and historical-vintage behavior must be demonstrated before any G2 use.

sources.source_title: Statistical Summary of Commercial Jet Airplane Accidents
sources.observed_granularity: annual worldwide all-commercial-jet departures/flight-hours plus cumulative Boeing/type statistics
sources.reason: No complete annual Boeing-family departures/cycles matrix for the required 2010-2025 cohort-year cells has been demonstrated. Aggregate fleet totals and cumulative type rates cannot be inverted or disaggregated into family-year exposure. Boeing's current summary cites Jet Information Services for 2005-2019 aggregate fleet activity and Cirium for 2020-2025 aggregate fleet activity, reinforcing that authoritative global operational exposure is sourced from specialized data providers rather than recoverable from the public aggregate chart.

sources.publisher: U.S. Department of Transportation / Bureau of Transportation Statistics
sources.observed_granularity: monthly non-stop segment records by aircraft type/service class with scheduled/performed departures and aircraft hours
sources.reason: The database covers U.S. domestic operations and international operations with at least one U.S./territory service point; foreign-to-foreign flights are excluded. It can support sensitivity/reconciliation work but cannot serve as the global BSFM family-year denominator.

sources.source_title: ICAO Long Term Traffic Forecast application
sources.observed_granularity: historical traffic by carrier/country-pair/route-group/region plus forecasts of departures and fleet forecasts by aircraft type
sources.reason: The public product description does not establish a reproducible historical actual-departures matrix at Boeing-family-by-year granularity matching the BSFM denominator. Forecasted departures/fleet are not substitutes for historical measured exposure, and no new ICAO API retrieval is permitted.

vintage_policy_requirement.reason: Historical exposure may be revised. Any baseline must declare whether it uses contemporaneous published vintages or a fixed versioned modern reconstruction and must not mix those objects silently.

prohibited_transformations: allocate aggregate departures to Boeing families using fleet share
split Boeing 737 all-variant sectors into Original/Classic/NG/MAX using fleet share, deliveries, market share or accident counts
invert cumulative accident rates to reconstruct annual family departures
use fleet counts, deliveries, capacity or market share as the primary denominator
substitute forecast departures for historical measured departures
mix revised modern historical sector values with contemporaneous-vintage values without a declared version policy

conclusion.next_research_direction: The remaining G2 problem is now primarily lawful data access plus product-scope validation, not public-source discovery. Obtain a representative licensed extract/data dictionary from OAG, Cirium or WATS and run the fixed acceptance contract. If no such access is available, retain G2 BLOCKED or prospectively version a different cohort/baseline design; do not proxy-split the current cohorts.
